items.t: The City plans the south side in separate schedules: Schedule B5 is Sardis and Schedule B6 is South Vedder in the 2050 Official Community Plan (Official Community Plan Bylaw 2025, No. 5500) — which schedule a specific Vedder Mountain parcel falls in is a per-parcel check.
Sunnyside Boulevard at Cultus Lake carries the nearest district school to the mountain's west side: Cultus Lake Swílhcha Community School at 71 Sunnyside Blvd, Cultus Lake.

Vedder Road is the north–south road at the mountain's foot: British Columbia Transit (BC Transit) Route 51 Vedder runs on Vedder Road between Downtown Chilliwack and the University of the Fraser Valley Chilliwack campus.

The one named institution on the mountain's Cultus Lake side is residential in character: Cultus Lake Swílhcha Community School, 71 Sunnyside Blvd, is a public elementary school in School District No. 33 (Chilliwack).

blocks.text: Vedder Mountain: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Slope is the trigger: Development Permit Area 5 (Hillside Development) applies to all lands within the City of Chilliwack with slopes of 20 percent or more, and a Development Permit is required before subdivision, construction or land alteration inside a designated area unless an exemption applies.

Development Permit Area 2 (Hillside and Upland Areas) protects development from hazardous hillside conditions and environmentally sensitive areas, and a geotechnical report from a qualified professional is required with each Development Permit Area 2 application.

Development Permit Area 1 covers the City's drinking-water supply lands — the municipal watersheds and aquifers — which is the permit area to check on upland parcels above the city's water supply areas.
Development Permit Area 3 protects riparian areas and fish habitat on creek crossings, which matters on the mountain's creek lots.

blocks.text: Vedder Mountain: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: A building permit here can carry a geotechnical condition a flatland lot never sees: construction on land that may be subject to flooding, mud flows, debris flows, erosion, land slip, rockfalls, subsidence or avalanche may not be permitted unless a report certified by a registered professional geotechnical engineer states the land may be safely used as intended.

Hillside neighbourhoods are Wildlife Issue Areas for garbage: the City designates hillside areas including Chilliwack Mountain and Little Mountain, where carts may not go to the curb before 5:00 a.m. on collection day and wildlife-resistant carts are required from May 1, 2026 — whether a specific Vedder Mountain street is designated is a check on the City page.

One cost is hillside-specific in kind, not in a published fee: a Development Permit Area 2 application requires a geotechnical report from a qualified professional, which the applicant commissions — no City fee figure for that report exists, and none is stated.
Route 51 Vedder is the transit spine at the mountain's foot, running Downtown Chilliwack to the University of the Fraser Valley Chilliwack campus via Vedder Road.
Downtown Chilliwack is the exchange where Route 51 connects to the rest of the BC Transit Chilliwack system, including Route 66 Fraser Valley Express.

blocks.text: Vedder Mountain: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check slope before anything else: Development Permit Area 5 applies at slopes of 20 percent or more anywhere in the city, and Development Permit Area 2 requires a geotechnical report with the application.
Check the floodplain at the mountain's foot: Floodplain Regulation Bylaw 2018, No. 4519 sets the 75-metre Vedder River setback and the flood construction levels shown on its Schedule A map.
Check drinking-water lands: Development Permit Area 1 covers the surface water supply areas for the City of Chilliwack, and its checklist must accompany a permit application on those lands.
Check riparian creeks: Development Permit Area 3 protects fish and fish habitat and riparian areas on creek-crossed lots.

faq.q: Does my lot's slope change what I can build?
faq.a: Yes — at 20 percent slope a second permit layer applies. Development Permit Area 5 covers all City of Chilliwack land with slopes of 20 percent or more, and Development Permit Area 2 can also apply to hillside and upland land, with a geotechnical report required from a qualified professional as part of the application, before subdivision, construction or land alteration proceeds.

faq.q: Which elementary school serves the Cultus Lake side of the mountain?
faq.a: The school located there is Cultus Lake Swílhcha Community School at 71 Sunnyside Blvd, Cultus Lake, a public elementary school in School District No. 33.

faq.q: What flood rules apply near the Vedder River at the mountain's foot?
faq.a: The City's floodplain bylaw sets the setback from this river. Floodplain Regulation Bylaw 2018, No. 4519 sets a minimum setback of 75 metres from the natural boundary of the Vedder River and 30 metres from the Chilliwack River and Vedder Canal for buildings requiring floodproofing, with floor levels set by the flood construction level.

faq.q: Can I book a private showing with Jared?
faq.a: Yes. Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, books private showings across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361, or use the contact form on this site.
